remote-runner-setup.title: Another machine: prepare, report and receive tasks
remote-runner-setup.intro: Run these commands manually on the target machine, then return to the original quick connection flow. Reporting with a paired identity still requires an explicit safe control URL and the current project. Preparation, pairing, reporting and enablement remain separate steps.
remote-runner-setup.public_only: Enter only public identifiers and absolute paths on the target machine. The browser does not read credentials, install programs or run copied commands.
remote-runner-setup.field.control: Control URL reachable from the target machine
remote-runner-setup.field.worker: Worker ID registered in that project
remote-runner-setup.field.state: Absolute path to the original Runner journal directory
remote-runner-setup.field.repository: Absolute Git repository root on the target machine
remote-runner-setup.field.baseCommit: Fixed baseline commit (full 40 or 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters)
remote-runner-setup.field.identityPath: Absolute path to the approved public identity file
remote-runner-setup.paired_help: Use the same pairing ID on the target machine to locate its existing default identity file. The Runner checks the exact control URL, project and Worker. A custom identity path can be selected explicitly in the identity-file mode; no replacement identity is created.
remote-runner-setup.incomplete.paired: Choose the target shell and complete the safe control URL, current project, approved pairing ID, exact Worker, configuration, repository and fixed baseline to copy the report command.
remote-runner-setup.target_hint: Continuing the original approved node in this project. Its service, project, pairing and Worker are fixed. Choose the target shell and local paths to prepare, report or explicitly start that node.
remote-runner-setup.invalid_target: This approved node does not match the current project or its source is invalid. Return to the original pairing record and read it again.
remote-runner-setup.pair_intro: This machine has no node identity yet? Use the original project administrator's pairing review without typing a Worker ID or pasting a token.
remote-runner-setup.identity_help: Use the original identity file confirmed by the target terminal and explicitly enter the current safe control URL. The project is fixed to the currently loaded project, rather than the manual credential draft. The Runner checks that the URL and project match the original identity. Worker and secret come from that identity and the system credential store; no manual Worker or pasted token is needed. Its independent default journal is used. Pairing does not prepare, report or execute tasks automatically.
remote-runner-setup.shell_help: Explicitly choose the remote PowerShell or Bash shell. The browser's operating system does not select the remote shell.
remote-runner-setup.prepare.title: Prepare local configuration
remote-runner-setup.prepare.intro: Install and configure suma-runner and the development tools according to their own requirements first. Choose a configuration file that does not yet exist; preparation does not overwrite files.
remote-runner-setup.prepare.boundary: Only fixed commands that can actually launch are prepared automatically. Codex App Server, Qoder, Cursor Agent, Claude SDK and OpenCode need their own complete configuration. Installation detection, configuration drafts and copied commands do not establish a connected node or dispatch eligibility. No empty configuration is created when nothing can be prepared.
remote-runner-setup.cursor.title: Configure Cursor Agent on the target machine
remote-runner-setup.cursor.intro: Cursor Agent requires a reviewed Node package, an explicit version, model and credential reference. Enter the target machine's details in its configuration form, then prepare the file manually.
remote-runner-setup.cursor.configuration: Return to the same Cursor Agent configuration form and choose the target shell and configuration file path. The returned draft fills only these three fields, preserving the node identity, repository and baseline. The file still needs to be explicitly created on the target machine.
remote-runner-setup.claude_sdk.title: Configure Claude SDK on the target machine
remote-runner-setup.claude_sdk.intro: Claude SDK requires fixed Node, a reviewed host, the native CLI, an exact model ID and a credential environment reference. Enter the target machine's details in its configuration form, then prepare a new file manually.
remote-runner-setup.claude_sdk.configura: Return to the same Claude SDK configuration form to generate a command draft. The returned tool, shell and configuration file path preserve the node identity, repository and baseline. The file still needs to be explicitly created on the target machine.
remote-runner-setup.report.title: Report tool inventory once
remote-runner-setup.report.intro: Enter the original project and Worker identity. This command does not create identities or claim tasks. Use HTTPS; HTTP is allowed only for loopback addresses.
remote-runner-setup.loopback: A loopback URL points to the machine running this command. To reach a control service on another machine, use an HTTPS URL reachable from the target machine.
remote-runner-setup.token_help: Securely set the registered Worker's SUMA_RUNNER_TOKEN in the target process environment first. The command checks only for its presence; it contains and displays no token value. Keep the original journal directory for retries.
remote-runner-setup.baseline_help: Probing writable development tools requires a real Git repository and a complete fixed baseline. The original Runner checks the repository and isolated worktree conditions. Entering a baseline does not establish reported inventory or a started task.
remote-runner-setup.report.boundary: --allow-exec permits probing fixed local programs and protocols. The command exits after reporting. An unconfirmed inventory receipt is reconciled as the same operation first; no persistent Runner or development task is started.
remote-runner-setup.reuse.title: Reuse the result through quick connection
remote-runner-setup.reuse.intro: Select that exact Worker in the current project's tool connection flow, read inventory again, and choose the complete fixed configuration. Open or explicitly choose an existing matching profile. Do not register the same identity again.
remote-runner-setup.enable.title: Explicitly review and enable
remote-runner-setup.enable.intro: New profiles remain paused. Check permissions, tool version, workspace and original configuration, then explicitly enable through the existing confirmation flow. Fresh inventory does not establish model sign-in, budget availability or accepted task delivery.
remote-runner-setup.start.title: Start receiving authorized tasks
remote-runner-setup.start.intro: Reuse the identity, configuration and fixed repository baseline entered above. After reviewing and enabling the profile, run this separate command on the target machine to keep the original Runner available for authorized tasks.
remote-runner-setup.start.boundary: Keep the target terminal running. Check the original node and run pages for actual online and execution status. Copying the command does not start a Runner in the browser.
remote-runner-setup.incomplete.start: Complete the identity and tool-reporting fields above to copy the startup command. No additional paths or credentials are needed.
remote-runner-setup.incomplete.prepare: Choose the target shell and enter a valid absolute JSON file path to copy the preparation command.
remote-runner-setup.incomplete.report: Complete the safe control URL, exact project and Worker IDs, configuration and journal paths, Git repository root and full fixed baseline to copy the one-shot report command.
remote-runner-setup.incomplete.identity: Enter the safe control URL, confirm the current project is loaded, and complete the absolute approved identity, configuration and Git repository paths plus the full fixed baseline to copy the one-shot report command.
remote-runner-setup.copy_failed: Could not copy. Select the command text and copy it manually.
remote-runner-setup.special.title: Prepare the selected protocol
remote-runner-setup.special.intro: {{tool}} needs its dedicated configuration before this same node reports or starts.
remote-runner-setup.special.configuratio: Use the tool's configuration guide, then return with the prepared commands file. Generic tool preparation cannot create this protocol's configuration.
remote-runner-setup.allow_discovery: Allow installed-tool detection on this node
remote-runner-setup.allow_discovery_help: Explicitly opt in to bounded installation checks. The standalone command starts an authenticated maintenance-only node and does not receive new development tasks. It does not install or enable tools.
remote-runner-setup.incomplete.discovery: Choose an identity mode and enter the control URL and identity path, or the current project, node and state directory. No repository or tool configuration file is needed.
